label: u/g/b/p or <DEL> input in sequences starting with v/n/j/1/c
explanation: Fires almost only in the original and delimiter phases (99.9% of mass) and never at t<2 or in the copy phase. It depends on the current input token: u (8.6x lift, 36% of mass, gives the largest activations), <DEL> (29% of mass), then g/b/p and w more weakly. q and the digits 0 and 3 almost never fire. Activity is much higher when the first original token is v/n/j/1/c (about 4x lift). It is strongest at t=3-4 and on first occurrences of a token. The conjunction captures only about 62% of mass with precision about 0.27. Many activations fall outside these sets, and many matching steps stay silent, so the true dependence on sequence history is more distributed than this rule. No single clean predicate was found.
